question: For a group ride, the lead rider and sweep rider should be:
choice_a: The most experienced riders of the group
explanation: The lead rider and sweep rider should be the most experienced riders in the group; the lead looks ahead for changes and signals early, and the sweep sets the pace from the rear.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.42, 'Plan'

question: Inexperienced riders in a group should be positioned:
choice_a: At the very back of the group
choice_c: In the middle, riding alongside another rider
explanation: Place inexperienced riders just behind the leader so they don't have to chase the group, and more experienced riders can watch them from behind.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.42, 'Plan'

question: The most important rules for group riding, per the manual, include:
choice_a: The fastest rider should always lead
choice_c: No competition, no passing of other riders, and no tailgating
choice_d: Riders should switch positions every five minutes
explanation: The most important group riding rules are: no competition, no passing of other riders, and no tailgating.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.42, 'Plan'

question: In staggered formation, the group leader rides in which position of the lane?
explanation: The group leader rides on the left side of the lane, and the second rider stays at least one second back on the right side of the lane.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.42, 'Staggered Formation'

question: In staggered formation, the second rider should follow the first rider by at least:
choice_a: One second, on the opposite side of the lane
choice_b: Five seconds, in the same lane position
explanation: The second rider stays at least one second back and rides on the right side of the lane, while the third rider keeps at least two seconds behind the first on the left side.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.42, 'Staggered Formation'

question: It is best to shift from staggered to single-file formation when:
choice_b: Riding in curves, turning, or entering/leaving freeways
choice_c: Riding on a wide, straight rural road
explanation: It is best to move to single-file formation when riding in curves, turning, and entering or leaving freeways or highways.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.42, 'Staggered Formation'

question: Riders should never ride directly alongside another rider in the same lane because:
choice_a: It is against the law in every state
choice_c: There is no place to maneuver if you must avoid a car or hazard
explanation: Never ride directly alongside another rider in the same lane; there is no place to go if you have to maneuver to avoid a hazard. Wait until both are stopped to talk.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.42, 'Do not Pair Up'

question: At an intersection with a left-turn arrow, the manual advises a group to:
choice_a: Split into pairs riding side-by-side through the turn
choice_b: Spread out as much as possible before turning
choice_c: Have every rider run the light together regardless of timing
choice_d: Tighten the formation and turn single file, not side-by-side
explanation: Tighten the formation to allow as many riders through as possible, making the turn single file, not side-by-side; if not everyone makes it, stop and wait ahead.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.43, 'Intersections'

question: On a two-lane highway, riders in a staggered formation who want to pass slower traffic should:
choice_b: Pass all at once, as a single unit
choice_d: Pass only the lead rider, leaving others behind
explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders in staggered formation should pass one at a time; the group may pass as a unit only on a freeway or interstate passing slow traffic.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.43, 'Passing in Formation'

question: According to the Ten Rules of Group Riding, the length of the route should be based on:
choice_b: The ability of the least experienced rider
choice_c: The rider with the largest fuel tank
explanation: Base the length of the route and segments on the ability of the least experienced rider.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.44, 'Ten Rules of Group Riding'

question: If a rider wants to ride faster than the pace of the group, the manual advises:
choice_a: The rider should tailgate the person ahead to encourage faster riding
choice_b: The whole group should speed up to match
choice_c: Riding ahead of the group instead of pressuring others
choice_d: The rider should be removed from the group permanently
explanation: Do not tailgate or encourage the rider in front to speed; if you want to ride faster, ride ahead of the group.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.44, 'Ten Rules of Group Riding'

question: When entering a freeway as a group, riders should:
choice_b: Wait for a complete gap in traffic before any rider enters
choice_c: Enter all at once, blocking the on-ramp
choice_d: Enter in single file and form up only after all riders have safely merged
explanation: Enter the freeway in single file and form up in staggered formation only after all riders have safely merged into traffic.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.43, 'Interstate Highways and Freeways'

question: The 'T-CLOCS' checklist is used by group riders before a long trip primarily to:
choice_a: Serve as a reminder of important components to check on the motorcycle
explanation: Use the T-CLOCS checklist as a reminder of the important components to check before leaving on a group ride.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.42, 'Preparation'

question: During a group ride, riders should use their mirrors to:
choice_b: Keep an eye on the rider behind and confirm the group is staying together
explanation: During the ride, use mirrors to keep an eye on the rider behind and confirm that the group is staying together; slow down if a rider falls behind.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.42, 'Follow those behind'
